messages.subject: OccuMulti
parts:
Hi all,
I am so happy I found this group! And apologies if the questions seem very basic, I am quite new to this area.

I have perused the documentation and online vignettes but I am still slightly unsure of an answer to my questions.

I want to run multi species occupancy models for 2 species (Jaguars and Pumas) with 8 env variables.

–––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––
Script:

df #dataframe
jag <- df$Jaguar #subset Jaguar presence/absence
pum<-df$Puma #subset Puma presence/absence
y2k<-list(matrix(jag),
          matrix(pum))

site2 <-df[,5:13] # extract covariates

# create unmarkedFrame for modelling 
CatOccupancy <-unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = y2k, siteCovs = site2, 
                                      obsCov = NULL)

# Up to this point all good.

#Length should match number/order of species in data@ylist 
# I have two species so: 
detFormulas <- c('~1','~1')

# Length should match number/order of columns in fDesign
occFormulas <- c('~canopy_cover','~1','~1')
# I am not sure how I can add more covariates to this part? I have 8 in total but keeps telling me I can only have 3 models.

#Look at output
fit:

Call:
occuMulti(detformulas = c("~1", "~1"), stateformulas = c("~1", 
    "~1", "~1"), data = CatOccupancy)

Occupancy:
                      Estimate  SE        z P(>|z|)
[sp1] (Intercept)       -0.282 171 -0.00165   0.999
[sp2] (Intercept)       -0.236 NaN      NaN     NaN
[sp1:sp2] (Intercept)    1.598 NaN      NaN     NaN

Detection:
                  Estimate  SE       z P(>|z|)
[sp1] (Intercept)     1.81 NaN     NaN     NaN
[sp2] (Intercept)     1.38 334 0.00415   0.997

AIC: 163.4548 

End of script
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Here I have NAs but I can't work out why?
- My data is made up of multiple locations, is there a way I can add that into the model?
- Do you have any advice for unit of replication for camera trap data? (5 days, 7 days, 1 day)
- Is what I have done make sense?

I am happy to email over my data and r script if it would help to answer my questions

All the best and thank you!
Mark

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: OccuMulti
parts:
Hi Mark,

I think there are some issues with how you constructed your unmarkedFrame. Your object y2k should be a list of matrices, each with #rows = #sites and #cols=#sampling occasions. It looks like you are just creating matrices directly out of data frame columns, which means you only have one column/one replicate sampling occasion per species, which isn't enough info and is likely causing the NaNs in your output. I would suggest taking a close look at the example for occuMulti and specifically what the structure of each part of the y-list looks like to make sure your data match. I think this will also get at your question about having multiple locations - each location should be a row in each of your species matrices and each column a replicate. So if you have 2 species, 10 sites, and 3 replicates per site, you'd end up with a y-list with two elements, each one a 10x3 matrix of 0s and 1s.

Regarding formulas, you can only have 3 state models (species 1, species 2, and species1+2 interaction), but each model can have one or more covariates. So to add more covariates it would look like:

occFormulas <- c('~canopy_cover + elevation + soil', '~soil', '~1')

Then the species 1 formula includes covariates for canopy cover, elevation, and soil, species 2 is just soil, and the interaction has no covariates. I would not suggest just throwing all 8 covariates in to all models right away though. Start simple (as you've done in your example) and build up complexity based on your specific hypotheses for this study.

It's hard to answer the question about unit of replication, since it depends on a lot of factors including the total length of your data collection period and how frequently each species is detected, and your goals. If you have a relatively long (weeks/months) data collection period and species are rarely detected, you may get better results  by using a longer unit of replication like a week. If your cameras are only open for a week or two and species are encountered very often, 1 day might be better. It also depends a lot on what kind of ecological questions you are asking. 

Ken

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: OccuMulti
parts:
I would start by keeping each camera separate so that you have 80. Whether the cameras are actually independent depends on how far apart they are, how much individuals of your species are moving, etc. Including a site/location covariate would be a good idea. The alternative (compressing to just 4 sites) is unlikely to work, it's just not enough data for this model which is pretty data-hungry.

The model assumes that the population is closed during the sampling period. This may not be true for your system over a time period as long as six months. You may want to consider using a shorter time period (i.e., a subset) of your full data during which you are confident the population was closed. Others with more experience using camera trap data may be able to provide better advice.

Ken
